rationale: Both passes produced the same type (follow_up), the same action (delete), and all-null temporal fields. They differ only in title fidelity: the first pass wrote 'Shopping task for project V4-NORMAL-003', preserving 'أغراض' (supplies) from the source, while the second wrote 'Project V4-NORMAL-003 task', dropping it. The first pass is canonical because it preserves the entity the source names. The decision flip (edited vs accepted) is genuine intra-reviewer noise: policy 1.0.0 never defined when a title rewrite requires 'edited'. Closed by rule EDIT-001 in policy 2.1.0.

Source 'תתקשר למאיה ותשלח את דוח פרויקט V4-NORMAL-039 מחר.' contains two commitments. The first pass accepted a single combined completion, which policy 1.0.0 permitted. The second pass rejected it with reason 'Multiple commitments are combined instead of separated and ordered', which is exactly rule MULTI-001 introduced by policy 2.0.0 between the two passes. This is a guideline change, not reviewer unreliability, so it is excluded from the reliability metric rather than counted as agreement. The second pass is canonical.

This source was annotated per-item twice under the same policy. The two annotations agree on commitment count, both segment boundaries, and every non-temporal slot; they differ on exactly one field. The first annotation set item 1 dueAt to 2026-07-30T03:38:00-04:00. The source's reference_time is 2026-02-06T17:00:00-05:00, so 'מחר' (tomorrow) resolves to 2026-02-07; 2026-07-30T03:38 is the annotation session's own wall clock. The annotation tooling defaulted the datetime control to now rather than resolving against the record's reference_time. The second annotation is canonical, but it corrects dueAt to null, which discards the stated date entirely because per-item schema 1.0.0 requires a clock time inside localTimeSpec and cannot express a date-only value. Neither annotation is usable Gold, so this source needs re-annotation once the schema can carry a date-only localTimeSpec. Closed by rules TIME-001 and TIME-002 in policy 2.1.0.

Source 'Call Maya and send the project V4-0454 report tomorrow. / تذكير مختصر / תזכורת V4-0454' contains two commitments. Same MULTI-001 shift as pilot-v4-review-hebrew-039: accepted as combined under policy 1.0.0, rejected under 2.0.0 with the identical reason. The second pass is canonical, and valid per-item Gold already exists for this source with no temporal fields, so no re-annotation is needed. Separately recorded as defect CAL-003: this source was categorised difficult_code_switching rather than multiple_commitments, which is why the blind sample drew only one multi-commitment item instead of two. Closed by rule CAT-001 in policy 2.1.0.
